text:
ozge: Hey folks — planning to be in Istanbul ~May 12 -> Jul 21 (~10 weeks). Want to check: do I need to file anything for benefits/visa, will WFH stipend continue (and how it's prorated), and what's the process to ship a second monitor (customs?) Also: I might meet a partner company for 1 day to sync — does that create any nexus risk? :flag-tr
people-ops: Thanks for flagging @ozge! Quick checklist: submit the Homebase Change form (https://redwood.company/forms/homebase) with dates and country, attach passport + flight, and indicate whether you want temporary shipping. Stipend: it continues for approved temporary remote; partial-month proration applies. Can you confirm whether you're keeping your SF residence for benefits?

tom-payroll: FYI payroll note — we typically keep people on USD payroll for short trips. If tax partner recommends EOR routing for Turkey we may temporarily change routing which affects withholding. Stipend proration example we use: `prorated = monthly_amount * (days_in_country / days_in_month)`.

global-benefits: Heads-up on medical: US group plans don't fully cover routine care abroad; emergencies may be covered. We can enroll you in the short-term travel medical rider if eligible. Pension/401k stays active while on USD payroll; if local social security is triggered we may need to pause or register. We'll confirm after tax/vendor check.

tax-eng: Short answer on nexus — a single partner meeting is low risk but not zero. Key factors: contract signing, recruiting activities, or sustained presence increase risk. Turkey has its own presence and payroll rules; 183 days isn't the only test. We'll run a quick nexus analysis with our external tax advisor after the form is in. Please flag if you'll sign any agreements or conduct sales pitches while there.

iit-ship: On shipping: temporary shipping cap for short trips is $1,500 (different from relocation cap). For monitors we need a commercial invoice/receipt for customs and a local delivery address. Open a ticket in `#it-ship` with asset tag and delivery details (we'll provide HS codes for customs). Note: customs duties might be payable locally — we can advise but employees often cover duties personally and submit receipts for reimbursement subject to policy.

people-ops-bot: Policy update: "Temporary Remote: Europe & EMEA" guidance added to policy hub — includes checklist (homebase form, passport, receipts) and examples of stipend proration: https://redwood.company/policies/temporary-remote-emea

ozge: I will keep SF apartment for benefits, not moving household goods. Monitor only. No contract signing or recruiting while there — just a short partner sync day and regular dev work. I'll submit the form now.

people-ops: Perfect. Action items: 1) @ozge submit Homebase Change form + passport/flight, 2) open `#it-ship` ticket for monitor (include asset tag + Istanbul address), 3) confirm USD payroll is OK (reply here), 4) tax-eng will run nexus check after form submission and report within 48 business hours.

tom-payroll: Confirmed — USD payroll is OK for the trip unless tax partner advises otherwise. We'll flag any withholding differences if routing changes.

people-ops: Thanks all — once form and `#it-ship` ticket are in we'll kick off benefit/ payroll/ tax checks. Closing loop here when tax-eng posts findings. :white_check_mark:
